overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how phenomenology moved into cognitive science. You'll be asked about Dreyfus's critique of symbolic AI and his model of skill acquisition, enactivism and 4E cognition, and neurophenomenology.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: What does Dreyfus's psychological assumption hold?

options.html: The brain works like a set of on/off switches
options.text: The brain works like a set of on/off switches
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on symbolic AI and the four assumptions.

options.html: The mind operates on information by formal rules
options.text: The mind operates on information by formal rules
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! On this assumption, human thinking is itself symbol processing.

options.html: All knowledge can be formalized by a machine
options.text: All knowledge can be formalized by a machine
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on symbolic AI and the four assumptions.

options.html: The world consists of independent, determinate facts
options.text: The world consists of independent, determinate facts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on symbolic AI and the four assumptions.

forms.stemHtml: How does a proficient performer differ from an expert in the Dreyfus model?

options.html: The proficient performer still decides what to do deliberately
options.text: The proficient performer still decides what to do deliberately
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The proficient performer sees the situation intuitively but still decides deliberately.

options.html: The proficient performer relies only on context-free rules
options.text: The proficient performer relies only on context-free rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five-stage model of skill acquisition.

options.html: The proficient performer feels no involvement in outcomes
options.text: The proficient performer feels no involvement in outcomes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five-stage model of skill acquisition.

options.html: The proficient performer can't recognize situational aspects
options.text: The proficient performer can't recognize situational aspects
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five-stage model of skill acquisition.

forms.stemHtml: What is the name for the problem, in AI research, of representing which facts do and don't change when an action is performed, without explicitly checking every fact? Enter two words.

options.html: frame problem
options.text: frame problem
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In its broader sense, it's the problem of limiting reasoning to what's relevant.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the relevance problem and its grounds in Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty.

forms.stemHtml: What is the "middle way" in The Embodied Mind?

options.text: A compromise between cognitivism and connectionism
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on The Embodied Mind and enaction.

options.html: Organism and world specify each other, with no fixed ground
options.text: Organism and world specify each other, with no fixed ground
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It rejects both realism and idealism.

options.html: A balance between meditation and laboratory science
options.text: A balance between meditation and laboratory science
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on The Embodied Mind and enaction.

options.html: The claim that the world is projected by the mind
options.text: The claim that the world is projected by the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on The Embodied Mind and enaction.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately state claims of autopoietic enactivism? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Living systems produce the components that produce them
options.text: Living systems produce the components that produce them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That's autopoiesis.

options.html: Things matter to an organism given its self-maintenance
options.text: Things matter to an organism given its self-maintenance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That's sense-making.

options.html: Life and mind share organizational features
options.text: Life and mind share organizational features
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Thompson calls this a deep continuity of life and mind.

options.html: Basic cognition involves no mental content at all
options.text: Basic cognition involves no mental content at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

options.html: Cognition is computation over symbolic representations
options.text: Cognition is computation over symbolic representations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the self-producing organization of a living system, which continually produces the components that produce it and maintains a boundary with its environment? Enter one word.

options.html: autopoiesis
options.text: autopoiesis
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Autopoietic enactivism grounds cognition in it.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

options.text: As a confusion that disappears on analysis

options.html: As a gap in method, not only in theory
options.text: As a gap in method, not only in theory

options.html: As proof that experience is non-physical
options.text: As proof that experience is non-physical
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Varela's neurophenomenology and mutual constraints.

options.html: As a problem that physics will soon solve
options.text: As a problem that physics will soon solve
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Varela's neurophenomenology and mutual constraints.

options.text: Attention turns from what is experienced to how

options.text: The slowness of EEG compared with brain imaging

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately describe micro-phenomenology? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It focuses on a single, specific experience
options.text: It focuses on a single, specific experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! General descriptions tend to report beliefs about experience.

options.html: It steers attention from what to how an experience unfolded
options.text: It steers attention from what to how an experience unfolded
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Questions ask what came first and what was felt where.

options.html: It uses open questions to avoid suggesting content
options.text: It uses open questions to avoid suggesting content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The interviewee's own words are used.

options.html: It asks participants to rate experiences on a fixed scale
options.text: It asks participants to rate experiences on a fixed scale
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on micro-phenomenology and criticisms of neurophenomenology.

options.html: It records brain activity during the interview
options.text: It records brain activity during the interview
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on micro-phenomenology and criticisms of neurophenomenology.

forms.stemHtml: How does the epistemological assumption differ from the psychological assumption?

options.html: It concerns the brain's hardware, not the mind
options.text: It concerns the brain's hardware, not the mind

options.text: It claims that people consciously follow rules

options.html: It claims only that a machine could use the rules
options.text: It claims only that a machine could use the rules

options.html: It concerns what the world is made of
options.text: It concerns what the world is made of

forms.stemHtml: Why did "Heideggerian AI" fail, according to Dreyfus's 2007 essay?

options.html: It relied too heavily on explicit symbolic rules
options.text: It relied too heavily on explicit symbolic rules
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Heideggerian AI and the debate over learning systems.

options.html: It responded to fixed features and didn't learn
options.text: It responded to fixed features and didn't learn
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It avoided the frame problem only by never facing an open, changing world.

options.html: Its robots were too slow to act in real time
options.text: Its robots were too slow to act in real time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Heideggerian AI and the debate over learning systems.

options.html: It misread Heidegger's account of anxiety
options.text: It misread Heidegger's account of anxiety
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Heideggerian AI and the debate over learning systems.

forms.stemHtml: What is Dreyfus's term for skilled, fluid activity that responds to the situation without explicit rules, deliberation, or mental representations? Enter two words.

options.html: absorbed coping
options.text: absorbed coping
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Dreyfus argued that "Heideggerian AI" lacked it.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Heideggerian AI and the debate over learning systems.

forms.stemHtml: On sensorimotor enactivism, why do you experience a tomato as whole when you see only its front?

options.text: The brain builds a complete internal model of it

options.html: You know how moving would bring its back into view
options.text: You know how moving would bring its back into view
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Perceptual presence, on this view, is a kind of access.

options.html: You infer the back from memories of past tomatoes
options.text: You infer the back from memories of past tomatoes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

options.html: The tomato's back is projected onto it by the mind
options.text: The tomato's back is projected onto it by the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are conditions Clark and Chalmers place on extended belief? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The resource is reliably available and typically consulted
options.text: The resource is reliably available and typically consulted
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is part of the "glue" that couples it to the person.

options.html: Its information can be retrieved easily
options.text: Its information can be retrieved easily
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Using it is as easy as recalling.

options.html: The person automatically endorses what they retrieve
options.text: The person automatically endorses what they retrieve
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the "trust" condition.

options.html: The resource must be implanted in the body
options.text: The resource must be implanted in the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on objections and tensions in 4E cognition.

options.html: The resource must produce its own components
options.text: The resource must produce its own components
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on objections and tensions in 4E cognition.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the law-like ways in which sensory stimulation changes as a perceiver moves, or as objects move relative to the perceiver? Enter two words.

options.html: sensorimotor contingencies
options.text: sensorimotor contingencies

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on autopoietic, sensorimotor, and radical enactivism.

options.text: Neural data correct reports, but reports never guide analysis

options.html: Reports guide analysis, but data never change reports
options.text: Reports guide analysis, but data never change reports

options.html: Each guides and refines the other, in both directions
options.text: Each guides and refines the other, in both directions

options.html: Neither constrains the other; they run in parallel
options.text: Neither constrains the other; they run in parallel
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Varela's neurophenomenology and mutual constraints.

forms.stemHtml: How did Varela treat Husserl's epoché?

options.text: As a method replaced by brain imaging

options.text: Activity identical to the unreadiness trials

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are replies neurophenomenologists give to their critics? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Their methods train introspection rather than rely on it naively

options.html: Open questions limit the risk that reports are shaped
options.text: Open questions limit the risk that reports are shaped

options.html: Checks against neural and behavioral data limit the risk
options.text: Checks against neural and behavioral data limit the risk

options.html: Introspection is infallible when done carefully
options.text: Introspection is infallible when done carefully
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on micro-phenomenology and criticisms of neurophenomenology.

options.html: Small samples are a strength, not a limit
options.text: Small samples are a strength, not a limit

options.text: Planets fit equations without solving them

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately describe objections or tensions within 4E cognition? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Causal coupling doesn't show a resource is cognitive

options.text: Enactivists say extended functionalism only relocates cognition
